From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Internal: SpectraMed - draft sizing options and ramp (for review)

Team — drafting three distinct options to present to SpectraMed (Conservative / Balanced / Accelerated). Notes and assumptions are inline. Please review tradeoffs and cost notes before I send to Alex.

Assumptions (from Alex + prelim matrix):
- Peak traffic concentrated 9am-6pm PT weekdays; 60% of daily volume in 8-hour window.
- Mix: 70% 7B path (low-latency), 30% 70B path (high-quality).
- Average output tokens: 80 tokens/request for summarization; 30 tokens/request for chat.
- Target latency: 7B p95 <= 100ms; 70B p95 <= 500ms (best-effort).

Draft options (GPU estimates reflect equivalent A100-ish capacity; well normalize by model variant):

1) Conservative (lower capex commitment / higher burst reliance)
- Minimum committed GPUs: 12 (mixed-purpose lanes)
- Warm standby / burst: +24 GPUs on demand (best-effort, higher cost)
- Expected p95 (7B): ~95ms if prefix caching enabled; 70B path may see 400-800ms during spikes
- Ramp schedule: Month 0 (PO) reserve 12, Month 1 add 8, Month 3 add 8 if traffic trending as forecast
- Pros: low upfront commitment; Cons: higher risk on peak days and burst price volatility

2) Balanced (recommended for most customers)
- Minimum committed GPUs: 24
- Warm standby: +12 GPUs for burst and canary lanes
- Expected p95 (7B): ~70-90ms; 70B: ~300-450ms
- Ramp schedule: Month 0 reserve 24, Month 2 add 8, Month 4 add 8
- Includes 2-week canary window and model-variant fallback (quantized 70B)

3) Accelerated (aggressive for immediate scale + SLA headroom)
- Minimum committed GPUs: 40
- Warm standby: +8 GPUs for short bursts
- Expected p95 (7B): ~50-75ms; 70B: ~200-350ms
- Ramp schedule: Month 0 reserve 40, Month 1 add 8 for throughput tuning
- Pros: strong SLA headroom and reduced burst costs; Cons: higher monthly commitment

Cost guidance: ballpark unit economics (tokens) are sensitive to batching and KV caching. For the Balanced option we estimate incremental monthly spend ~ $Xk-$Yk (detailed numbers to be added in final doc).

Risks / mitigations:
- Cold-starts for 70B on first requests: mitigate with KV pre-warm and short lived "warm pools" during rollout.
- If client requires <100ms for 70B path, call out that quantized variants or model distillation will be required.

Please flag any redlines. Im planning to include a recommended canary plan and a DocuSign PO link in the external proposal.

Thanks,
Irene

From: marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>

Irene — quick thoughts:

- Add a "safety burst" cushion in the Balanced option that can be used for predictable weekly surges (e.g., backup clinics run heavy loads). Make it an explicit short-burst contract (6 hours/day) to bound cost.
- Include a fallback model variant for the 70B path (8-bit quantized) in the proposal and call out expected quality delta in the appendix.
- Call out canary gating: 25% traffic first 2 weeks, then 60% next 2 weeks, full cutover after metrics pass.
- For procurement: include a clause about 30-day traffic reforecast windows so they can add GPUs without renegotiating baseline pricing.

I'll add a brief cost-per-token estimate range for each option (still approximate). Good to include a recommended selection heuristic (start Balanced, move to Accelerated if 60%+ of forecast realized by month 2).

Marissa
